description: Top-of-page strips and mid-page promo bars. For a trade business they carry storm or emergency notices, seasonal offers (tune-up specials), financing, new locations or hiring, without looking like an ad or breaking the header.
queries: announcement bar at top of website
promo banner with limited time discount offer
alert notice banner for urgent service update

references.layout: A black band (~64px tall) directly under a black nav, so the two read as one header block. One centered line of text with a red-orange rounded button inline to its right. The hero photo starts immediately below.
references.type: Neo-grotesk light, ~18px, white, sentence case: 'Support for homeowners in fire-affected Southern California communities'. Button label sans ~12px.
references.color: Black ~#000000, white text, CTA ~#FF4A1C (the only red on the page).
details: Same color as the nav, so it extends the header instead of sitting on it like a sticker
Calm, specific wording about a crisis, no exclamation marks
A taller band than a typical strip gives it the weight of a real notice
references.why_it_works: It gives an emergency or community message gravity without an alarm-red full bar, and stays on-brand.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofer or restoration company after a storm: 'Storm damage in Linn County? Emergency tarping crews are available now.' [Get help today]. Shown only while active.

references.layout: A thin full-width bar (~22px) with one centered line: event name, a small inline brand glyph, then the offer. The nav and hero sit below on off-white.
references.type: Sans ~11px. Event name regular, offer bold ('The New Year's Sale ● Save up to 40%').
references.color: Pale chartreuse ~#DDF5A0, dark green ink ~#173A1E. The tint matches the brand's green accent.
details: Bold is used only on the number
An inline brand glyph acts as the separator instead of a pipe or dash
The light tint reads as friendly, not as an ad
references.why_it_works: Soft color, one fact in bold and no button. It informs without fighting the hero.
references.trade_adaptation: HVAC: 'Fall furnace tune-up ● $89 through Oct 31' on a pale tint of the brand color, with the whole bar linking to booking.

references.layout: A thin electric-blue bar (~16px). The message is left-aligned ('Free standard shipping on orders $40+'). On the right are tiny ‹ › arrows and a ⏸ pause control for the rotating messages.
details: Rotation has accessible manual controls, including pause
Left alignment matches the nav grid instead of floating centered
Very short copy (under 40 characters)
references.why_it_works: It lets a business rotate three useful facts in one slim strip and stays accessible.
references.trade_adaptation: Rotate: 'Financing from $0 down' / '24/7 emergency line (555) 012-3456' / 'Now booking spring cleanups', in the brand's strongest color.

references.layout: A beige bar (~22px) with tiny centered text ending in an underlined link. A transparent nav floats over the full-bleed photo hero below.
references.type: Sans ~10px, ink. The link is underlined, not a button ('Get updates from Rivian.').
references.color: Beige ~#E8E3D3, ink ~#222222. The tone matches the dusty landscape photo.
details: The bar color is pulled from the hero photo palette
The link is an underline, not a button
It asks a question first ('Want to see what we're up to?')
references.why_it_works: Low-key and harmonious. It never competes with a strong photo hero.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Now scheduling winter roof inspections. Book a slot.' in a sand tone that matches a warm exterior photo.

references.layout: A yellow bar (~22px) split into three slots on the nav grid: brand tagline left ('Transforming Spaces, Driving Growth'), a priced offer centered ('Subscription solutions for offices, from 49kr/m²'), language selector right.
references.type: Sans ~10px, dark ink. Uses a real superscript for m².
details: Three slots give credibility, offer and utility a fixed place each
The price is in the middle, so the eye lands on it
Strong brand color, used nowhere else in large areas
references.why_it_works: It uses the strip as information architecture instead of a single shout.
references.trade_adaptation: Left 'Family-owned since 1976', center 'Water heater installs from $1,199', right '(555) 012-3456' as a tap-to-call link.

references.layout: A thin bar (~18px) with several short announcements scrolling horizontally, each ending in → and separated by small emoji. It sits above a nav on a light pink dotted-grid background.
details: Multiple updates without a carousel UI
Monospace gives it a teletype or news-wire feel
Each item is a link with its own arrow
references.why_it_works: It fits several small items of news (hiring, reviews, new area) into one quiet strip with personality.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Now hiring apprentices → · 4.9★ on Google (412 reviews) → · Now serving Round Rock →' in mono on a pale brand tint. Pause on hover.

references.layout: A pale blue bar (~22px) with centered content: megaphone icon, one sentence, and a small white 'Learn more →' pill. A × close sits at the far right.
references.color: Pale blue ~#D6E9FF, navy ~#0B2A4A, white pill with a hairline border.
details: Close affordance for non-critical news
A small icon frames it as an announcement
The pill CTA is visually lighter than the main nav CTA
references.why_it_works: Polite, clear and closable. It sets the template for non-urgent news.
references.trade_adaptation: '📣 We've moved to a bigger shop on Main St. [See hours →] ×', with the dismissal remembered in localStorage.

references.layout: A horizontal inset card (~600×70) within the content width. Left: a mascot illustration holding a '100' sign. Center: serif headline 'Unlimited Access', then an offer line with a struck-through old price and the new price in bold, and a gift line. Right: wordmark, black 'Subscribe' button, and tiny 'Cancel or pause anytime.' underneath.
references.type: Serif headline ~18px. Sans body ~11px. The old price uses strikethrough ('$2.50' → '$1 a week').
references.color: Cream ~#F6EFD9, black ink and button, illustration in black line with a red accent.
details: Strikethrough price makes the deal concrete
Reassurance microcopy under the button
The illustration gives it a print-ad charm
references.why_it_works: It feels like a crafted print ad, not a web banner, and the price mechanics are persuasive.
references.trade_adaptation: Mid-page: 'Gutter guard install: ~~$1,400~~ $1,050 this month, plus a free cleaning.' [Claim offer] / 'No deposit needed.' with a line drawing of a house gutter.

references.layout: A wide rounded (~8px) band (~100px tall) inside the content width. Left: a small white tag chip ('SEV0'), a serif headline and an orange text link with an arrow. Right: four photos with rounded corners, tilted and fanned, overlapping each other and breaking out above the top edge of the band.
references.type: Serif regular ~22px white. Link sans ~12px. Tag chip mono/sans caps ~9px.
details: Photos break the container edge, which adds depth
Tag chip names the event or offer like a label
A text link instead of a button keeps it editorial
references.why_it_works: A promo band that feels like a magazine insert. The fanned photos add life without clutter.
references.trade_adaptation: 'SPRING EVENT · Free AC check with any service →' on a deep brand color, with fanned photos of real jobs and techs.

references.layout: Off-white section. Left: a tall stadium/oval photo mask (~300×540) of a canvas tote on a picnic blanket outdoors. Right: a centered serif headline '20% Off Reusables', a 3-line body, and an outlined pill 'Shop Sale'.
references.type: Display serif (soft, Recoleta/Tiempos feel) ~32px. Sans body ~12px. All type is one accent color.
references.color: Off-white ~#F7F5F0, red-orange ~#E8462B for every piece of type and the pill outline, natural photo greens and canvas.
details: Monochrome typography in a single accent color
The oval photo mask echoes the pill button shape
The discount is the headline, stated plainly
references.why_it_works: A sale that looks editorial instead of like a coupon. Shape and color discipline make it feel premium.
references.trade_adaptation: Painter: '15% off exterior painting' beside an oval photo of a freshly painted porch, with 'Book by May 1' and an outlined 'Get a quote' pill.

takeaways: Make the strip part of the header. Match the nav color (Samara) or use a muted tint pulled from the photo or brand (Rivian, Seed), not an unrelated bright.
One message, one link, under ~70 characters. Use an underlined link or a small pill; a full button is only for real emergencies.
Bold only the number or offer ('Save up to 40%', '$89').
Emergency or storm notices: use a taller dark band with calm, specific wording and one clear action. Don't shout in red caps.
Rotate or ticker only when there are 3+ genuinely useful messages, and give a pause control.
Mid-page promos should feel like print ads: strikethrough price, reassurance microcopy, an illustration or shaped photo, monochrome type in the accent color.
Non-critical news should be dismissible and remember that it was dismissed.
avoid: Fake OS warning dialogs and 'Claim Deal' pop-ups over synthwave graphics (beehiiv).
'LIMITED TIME OFFER!' in heavy caps with gimmick props (UGLYCASH CRT TV).
Sale banners on noisy multicolor gradients with huge '30% OFF' (SOTF).
Newsletter signup bands dressed up as announcements (Linear, PayPal 'Stay up to date', Dropbox 'Stay informed').
Countdown timers, flashing badges or fake scarcity. They read as untrustworthy for a local trade.
Gray utility strips crammed with icon + phone + email + hours + social icons all at 10px.
